chunks: Among them some will be unavenged martyrs and some will be stricken with fear and seek protection. They will be deceived by pledges and fraudulent belief.
You should not become landmarks of mischiefs and signs of innovations,
but should adhere to that on which the rope of the community has been wound and on which the pillars of obedience have been founded.
Proceed towards Allah as oppressed and do not proceed to Him as oppressors.
Avoid the paths of Satan and the places of revolt.
Do not put in your bellies unlawful morsels,
because you are facing Him Who has made disobedience unlawful for you, and made the path of obedience easy for you.

key_terms.مَطْلُول: Unavenged martyr (one who died but whose blood was not avenged)

ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical and social warnings given in this sermon from Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali contextualizes this advice within the early Islamic civil wars, warning against the hypocrisy of using religious oaths to mask political opportunism and social fragmentation. He establishes a theological framework where communal unity (jamāʿa) is the anchor of obedience, urging believers to prioritize divine justice by entering God's presence as the oppressed rather than the oppressors, thereby linking ethical consumption directly to spiritual accountability.
